turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'm Niamh, I'll do your checks before Dr Brennan sees you. Coat off the right arm there.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand. I'm wrecked and it's not even half ten.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 148 over 92. Pulse is 76. Oxygen is 98 percent. Have a seat, he's just finishing next door.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We were stuck on the M50 forty minutes. Some eejit with a trailer sideways at the Red Cow, and the rain bucketing.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): I told you to leave earlier. Don't start with me.

[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Your man on the radio said it's the worst August in years. Then Sean rang, the under twelves hurling is off, the pitch is a swamp. He wanted his grandad in the stand.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. Next week so. If the pitch dries.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello, sorry about the wait. I'm Dr Brennan. What has you in today?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): The hands. They go dead on me in the night, the thumb and the index and the middle finger. Both hands, the right is worse. Pins and needles, like, and I have to shake them out to wake them up.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): And shaking them brings the feeling back?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Give it a minute. It's driving me up the wall.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's dropping things as well. Dropped a cup of tea on Tuesday, all over the kitchen floor.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): One cup. Don't be making a show of me.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Is the job hard on the hands?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm on the packing line all day, gripping boxes. That's not helping, sure.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long has this been going on?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. About three months. Maybe a bit less.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ah no, Pat. It was on you before Christmas. Five months, easy.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not five months. I'd have said.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. You don't agree, so I'll note it as roughly three to five months and we won't fight the date.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): Is there pain in the hands, or is it just the numbness?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit of an ache in the right wrist in the morning. Not much. It eases once I'm up and moving.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the neck, or pain shooting down from the neck?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Neck's grand.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any weakness in the legs, or stumbling?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, or shortness of breath?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. I'm just tired from being woke up.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): And the waterworks, the bowels, all ticking over?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Of. Yeah. Grand. No bother there.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): What tablets are you on at the minute?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Err. Mizartan for the pressure. Forty milligrams I think, at night. And Omprazole twenty mg every morning for the heartburn.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The Mizartan isn't forty. I did the box on Sunday. It's 80.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it. I don't look. Whatever the chemist hands me. I miss it on the late shift, I'll say that.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): So the dose of the Mizartan isn't agreed and I won't guess it. The Omprazole twenty, that's every morning?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Every morning.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing.

[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll have a look at the hands now. Sensation is duller on the right thumb and index than on the little finger. There's no wasting of the muscles. Tinel's, tapping the right wrist, brings that tingle into the fingers, and the left is milder. Grip is a little down on the right. The neck moves freely and there's no pain when I press.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the exact night tingle. Ow. Can we move this on, I've a shift at two.

[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): So, to say it back. Both hands, the right worse, numb with pins and needles in the thumb, index and middle at night, you shake them awake, a morning ache in the right wrist, you dropped a cup, somewhere between three and five months. Mizartan for the pressure, dose not settled, missed on the late shifts, Omprazole twenty each morning for the heartburn. No neck pain, no chest pain, no weakness in the legs. Pressure today was 148 over 92.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): That's it. Yeah.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): I could reel off three or four things that do this pattern. I'm not going to pick one out today. Let's see what the tests say before anyone puts a name on it.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Get a wrist splint from the chemist, the right one at least, and wear it at night while you sleep. And ease off the heavy gripping on the line if they'll allow it.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): They won't love that. Fine. The splint, whatever.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Bloods on Thursday morning. Niamh will take a fasting glucose and a thyroid check. Nothing to eat or drink but water from midnight on Wednesday.
[SEG0047] person_1 (NURSE): Thursday, half eight, you're on my list. Fasting, water only.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back here in two weeks with those results.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): If it has not settled with the splint by then, we'll book a nerve conduction test. If those bloods are borderline, we'll add a B12. Not today.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll get the splint in the chemist on the way home. Come on, Pat, before that rain gets any worse.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Thursday, then two weeks. I just want a night's sleep.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Grand. Mind yourselves out there.

Ease off heavy gripping at work if allowed
Fasting glucose blood test, nothing to eat or drink but water from midnight

time_reference.value: if not settled with the splint in two weeks

The patient said Mizartan is forty milligrams but the family member said the box is 80 milligrams.
The patient says he misses Mizartan on late shifts, so nightly adherence is uncertain.

spec.situation: Middle-aged office or factory worker with night-time numbness in thumb, index and middle fingers, shakes hands to wake them; dropping cups; splint advice, nerve test conditional.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: The transcript looks like speech-to-text: drug names are sometimes spelled wrongly ('Omprazole', 'Mizartan' for telmisartan, 'Metformine'), fragments and fillers appear ('Err', 'Of.', 'Mm.', 'Umm'), numbers are sometimes digits and sometimes words.
traps.label_rule: Medicine names are recorded as written in the transcript (name) with a normalized/generic name ONLY when the true drug is certain from context (a drug 'for the pressure' written 'Mizartan' is NOT certain enough: leave generic_name empty). Fragments and fillers are never facts.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

omissions.text: No pain shooting down from the neck was specifically denied.
Positive Tinel's sign was stronger on the right and milder on the left, rather than simply positive at both wrists without laterality/detail.
Sensation was described as duller on the right thumb and index than on the little finger, not just reduced thumb and index sensation in isolation.
The doctor explicitly chose not to make a diagnosis yet and said he would wait for test results before naming the condition.
